notes: The author introduces exterior automorphisms of the profinite loop group indexed by (0,3), with an underlined marginal addition about the extension structure of E=E_{0,3}. He chooses generators l_0, l_1 and l_infinity with product 1, then describes endomorphisms through triples satisfying the same relation. This is a transcriptional account of his statements, not a verification of them.

The author’s explicit caution is “sauf erreur” before the assertion that the endomorphism is an automorphism when its images generate pi topologically. No date occurs on the sheet. The source contains [C], a circled 1, a separate upper-centre 1 and a lower-left 4; the relation of the two uncirculated pagination numbers is not inferred.

The page defines a cyclic permutation rho of the three generators, a transposition sigma_infinity and analogous sigma_0, sigma_1, and writes the conjugation relation rho sigma_i rho^{-1}=sigma_{rho(i)}. It then proposes an action respecting the structure of the loops with multiplier character 1 and states that there is already a true representation of the cyclic subgroup S_3^+ isomorphic to Z/3Z. The final sentence continues beyond this sheet.

No mathematical proof or group computation was performed in this reading. Mathematical context was used only to recognize the defined permutation-group notation and to flag difficult indices; it did not replace uncertain strokes with an expected symbol. The initial Pi/pi doubt was subsequently resolved for the explicit hatted title and its indexed group; the small unindexed prose pi and the unresolved style of S are kept distinct.

The three C deletion loci were separately examined: the title glyph remains unsure; the full line On s’intéresse aux is visibly struck through and remains deleted; the alleged l_0 deletion inside int is entangled with retracing and remains unsure. The exact layering of that last operand and the boundary between the struck title glyph and profini deserve root review. Neither was resolved merely because the live expression is mathematically familiar.

All five C insertion loci were checked for attachment. The int parenthesis is below the final sigma equality; the exchange parenthesis attaches after sigma_1; the S_3 attaches after groupe; caractère attaches immediately before multiplicateur; vraie attaches immediately before représentation. No additional diagram, drawing, date or marginal sentence was found.

Two small dark points beside the final prose pi were examined in crop 14. Their compact round forms are not prime strokes; the ordinary comma is separate below-right. The main reader treats these points as incidental ink, leaves the agreed unprimed pi, and records the observation here rather than inserting unsupported mathematical punctuation.

The first-pass images were consulted exactly once each: page.jpg for layout, top.png and bottom.png line by line. Fifteen first-reading crops were made, each for a distinct target or tightly related group; no OCR, external research, other scan, or other reader report was consulted. No TeX compilation was run.

The independent blind reading and root crop comparison resolve the two hatted title signs and the indexed endomorphism group as capital Pi. They also expose remaining uncertainty in the cramped de/du, the marginal index comma, the blackened second sigma index and the first exchanged-loop index. These are marked in place. Mathematical cyclicity makes the infinity/1 preferred readings coherent, but cannot resolve the overlapping ink. The later word calculation on scan006 is a check of that explicitly preferred cyclic system, not a resolution of these indices. A comma flagged by the second reader was already present in the page; several other differences were clipped excerpt boundaries or equivalent TeX wrappers.
